sections.name: assertionSchema, Assertion
sections.title: Shape of one literal field fact
sections.what: Defines the required shape for a single extracted fact: a field name and a non-empty value, plus optional unit, currency, date precision, price basis, milestone and number format.
sections.why: The header says the exact source wording is stored, and calculations are recorded separately.
sections.watch_out: Blank values are rejected, and an omitted date precision silently becomes not_applicable.

summary: Defines the required shape of one literal field fact, such as an owner name or a cost with its unit and currency.
purpose: Gives one set of rules that every extracted fact must follow before the system accepts it.
why: The header says normalisation and calculations are recorded separately, so the stored value stays the exact wording from the source.
how: Imports the schema library. Defines a schema listing each field and its rules. A value must have at least one character. Unit, currency, price basis, milestone and number format are optional. Date precision defaults to not_applicable. Exports a type so other code uses the same shape.
inputs: A candidate fact object from an extraction step.
outputs: A checked copy of the fact, or a validation error if a rule fails.
risks: Changing a field name or rule affects every collector that uses this shape. A blank value is rejected, which is correct but can stop a whole extraction if the rejection is not handled.
debug: If a fact is rejected, read the error for the field name. Compare the fact's keys and value with the rules listed in this file.
